title: The Ship in the Olive Grove
hook: A Norse longship lies upright in an olive grove, far above yesterday's shoreline. Its crew insists they sailed here. The harbor bell rings from beneath the new cliffs.
story: Alexios follows the stranded crew's account instead of treating them as raiders. A familiar coast ends at a cold-water channel that was not there the night before. The first discovery is geographical: the old maps are accurate, but no longer connect.
objectives: Reach the longship and rescue its survivors; their evidence is recorded permanently.
Investigate any two of three witnesses: drowned harbor, foreign cairn, or displaced creature meadow.
Secure First Harbor and establish a coastal signal visible from the northern fjord.
routes: A figure-eight around the olive heights: a short guarded cliff road, a longer productive farm valley, and a boat detour through the drowned harbor. The principal objective has two land approaches; the optional wreck requires sailing.
water: Teach embark/disembark with a supplied vessel and recoverable shipyard. The wreck expedition introduces water exploration without forcing a difficult sea battle in the first chapter.
choice: Salvage the stranded longship into a palisade (+one bounded defense reserve later), or preserve it as a refuge (+one bounded recruitment reserve). Either choice rescues the crew and advances the story.
mark: The cliff cut and drowned bell remain. The longship becomes either a timber memorial within the palisade or an inhabited refuge. First Harbor and its signal persist into P7.
later: In E1, Alexios finds the same ship ribs beneath a military checkpoint. The refuge version shelters evacuees; the palisade version offers a defensible side entrance.
ending: Hervor's chapter opens with Alexios's foreign signal visible across the fjord. Alexios: 'They have not crossed our border. Our border has crossed them.'
town: First Harbor, a new Greek frontier settlement using the existing Greek town kit.

title: A Warm Tide beneath the Ice
hook: Warm water pours under the fjord ice. A Greek signal burns beyond the mountains, and a rescued sailor carries news of a ship Hervor knows should be hundreds of miles away.
story: Hervor initially suspects an enemy rite. Exploring inland reveals that snowfields now end in another people's summer woodland. She secures an evacuation corridor and learns that several worlds have suffered the same wound.
objectives: Scout the broken fjord from either the high cairn or outer headland.
Establish Frostwatch and secure both ends of an evacuation route; progress follows secured sites, not fragile civilian escort units.
Clear a navigable approach toward the central sea and deliver a reply to First Harbor.
routes: A ring around the fjord: mountain switchbacks, two landings and a central frozen causeway. A warmed inlet becomes a permanent shortcut after a player-triggered event. No occupied tile disappears beneath a unit.
water: A ship is required to reach the far evacuation landing. The route can favor a guarded inner channel or longer outer water with salvage. One introductory single-ship creature battle uses a small ranged sea force.
choice: Open the western ice channel for safer shipping, or reinforce the eastern mountain road for land supply. Both remain viable in P7; the unimproved alternative stays slower, never impossible.
mark: The Broken Fjord contains visible floes and a marked shipping channel or reinforced pass. A rescued community establishes Frostwatch's refuge quarter.
later: E2 returns to the same broken ice channel, now watched by foreign blockade towers. The earlier improvement offers a real alternative approach.
ending: Hervor sends a rune-marked sounding weight south with a survey vessel. Seshet will find its report at an impossible river mouth.
target: 50–65 minutes; 3–4 required battles; first mandatory sailing.
town: Frostwatch, a Norse frontier hold distinct from the existing Winter Oath towns.

title: The River That Forgot the Sea
hook: The river flows inland at high tide. A northern survey vessel is trapped beside a desert obelisk, and its sounding weight carries Hervor's runes.
story: Seshet compares stars, current and old canal records. The river has acquired a new outlet into the shared basin. Saving the district requires deciding how to distribute water, not finding a villain to kill.
objectives: Read two river gauges in either order and recover the old canal plan.
Secure Sunbank and both sluice controls.
Choose an announced permanent water arrangement, then clear the reopened route to the central sea.
routes: A delta with three arms, island granaries, an inland caravan loop and a ridge road. A sluice choice alters two crossings while maintaining one all-weather land circuit and at least one navigable channel.
water: Ships carry the expedition to an island gauge and the basin outlet. The canal change previews affected cells and refuses activation while any stack would become stranded.
choice: Deepen the merchant canal for faster naval access, or restore the floodplain for a bounded food/recruitment benefit. Both options preserve a usable port and complete the mission.
mark: The Three-Mouth Delta gains a visibly deep canal or green reclaimed fields. Sluice position, shoreline and bridge foundations are permanent ledger entries.
later: In E3, the same gates have become weapons used to control other pantheons' food routes. The original canal choice changes which farms or shipping lane can be restored first.
ending: A carved Japanese lantern floats through the open channel. Seshet marks its course on the first map that includes another world's coast.
target: 55–75 minutes; 3–4 required battles; no unexplained countdown.
town: Sunbank, an Egyptian river settlement using existing town art.

title: Lanterns on a Foreign Shore
hook: Festival lanterns return against the current carrying desert reeds. One bears a charcoal map from Seshet. The drowned are following a coastline Akane has never seen.
story: Akane discovers that the paths of the dead are also displaced. She uses coastal landmarks to restore a safe local route, without solving the later Lantern Road campaign's separate crisis.
objectives: Establish Lantern Haven and recover the local shrine registers.
Visit any two of three islands to distinguish a safe channel from a false reflection.
Restore the paired shore lights and secure the island landing that joins the emerging shared chart.
routes: A triangular island network with a protected inner sea, dangerous outer channel and one neutral island port. Islands can be investigated in either order; lighthouse sight lines reveal useful navigation rather than a corridor of quest gates.
water: Ships are mandatory. One ship-versus-sea-creature battle uses the supplied deck/water layout. Any optional hostile ship encounter uses the separate two-ship boarding layout.
choice: Restore the nearer lighthouse for safe short crossings, or the outer lighthouse for a longer route that bypasses a hostile harbor. The unchosen route remains available with a disclosed extra cost or guard.
mark: Lantern Strait gains a permanent navigational light, repaired landing and memorial shore. The sea route is visible in P7 and on the later war map.
later: E5 begins where these same lights are being shuttered to intercept fleeing ships. A lighthouse originally built for lost souls now decides which living people escape.
ending: Akane sends the combined chart toward a grove whose trees have begun dropping salt-stained leaves.
target: 60–75 minutes; 4 required battles; guaranteed replacement ship access.
town: Lantern Haven, a frontier port, not a replacement for Kagaribi.

title: Roots beneath Foreign Stones
hook: An ancient oak lifts a stone bearing a foreign calendar. Animals flee toward the coast; one root has grown around a Japanese lantern that arrived with the chart.
story: Orla sees that the collision moved habitats as well as people. Local commanders are capturing displaced neutral creatures to build armies. She creates a migration corridor and learns that the most powerful commanders are gathering near the central island.
objectives: Locate two threatened habitats and secure Hazel Ford.
Open a viable migration corridor by controlling its endpoints and removing the trapping camp.
Recover the commanders' route orders and add the northeastern passes to the shared chart.
routes: Interlocking woodland and ridge circuits, two river crossings and a sheltered coastal bypass. Clearing a short root tunnel opens a useful back route. Neutral hiring sites are optional; they never supply a unique mandatory key.
water: A sea bypass can avoid the fortified ford at the cost of a ship encounter. An island grove provides optional recruits. Root-Runners, Baku and Afanc keep their existing movement traits; a wet habitat does not make them water-tile battle units.
choice: Make the recovered corridor a protected sanctuary for a later neutral reserve, or a public road for a later supply shortcut. Creatures survive in either outcome; this is a land-use decision, not a hidden moral trap.
mark: A conspicuous Living Arch connects the slopes. The protected route becomes a grove; the public route becomes a road with stone boundary markers. Captured pens remain as abandoned landmarks.
later: E4 returns to the same arch, now burned on one side and used as a frontier checkpoint. The earlier sanctuary/road changes the evacuation route.
ending: The recovered orders describe six commanders buying wild armies. Orla sends the evidence to Itzel's newly discovered southern observatory.
target: 55–75 minutes; 4 required battles; meaningful diplomacy alongside combat.
town: Hazel Ford, a new Celtic frontier fort.

title: The Night with Six Horizons
hook: The observatory records six incompatible star paths above one horizon. A northern tree root has split an old calendar stone, and Orla's orders describe armies gathering where the skies overlap.
story: Itzel proves that the foreign lands coexist now: this is not a dream, a temporary portal or an invading pantheon. The six commanders intend to control the crossings and drive the peoples apart using the creatures displaced by the collision.
objectives: Secure Ember Quay and observe two survey stations in either order.
Sail to the offshore observation isle and recover the complete horizon record.
Open the southern route to the central island and call the six heroes to a joint expedition.
routes: A volcanic horseshoe with two upland routes, a sheltered lake connected to the sea, an offshore station and two potential landing beaches. The volcanic rim is a fixed landmark; optional channel work creates a shortcut without deleting the longer approach.
water: Mandatory ocean crossing to the observation isle. A substantial but bounded Cetus or Isonade encounter tests sea combat. Do not require recruiting an aquatic unit to win.
choice: Restore the inland observatory for information about commander reserves, or the southern harbor stores for a bounded reinforcement package. Both reveal the proof and open the finale.
mark: The Six-Sky Observatory is repaired or its lower harbor becomes the expedition depot. A visible obsidian breach opens the southern channel. An empty six-seat council platform is built.
later: E6 returns to the same observatory to compare the original sky record with current fractures. The old depot or records change preparation, not access to the truth.
ending: The heroes meet for the first time. They agree to save travel and settlements, not to settle divine sovereignty. Itzel: 'Six skies. One shadow. Whatever happened, it happened to us together.'
target: 65–85 minutes; 4–5 required battles; reveal before finale.
town: Ember Quay, a Mesoamerican frontier port.

title: The First Accord
format: Six-hero campaign climax; sequential neutral warlords
hook: The shared chart is finally complete. Six commanders seize the crossings with enormous neutral armies, claiming that only their own people should control access to the new world.
story: The heroes' first alliance is practical: defeat the commanders, restore the routes and protect the frontier towns. They do not discover who caused the collision. The gods' arguments began during the first days; a renewed divine council after the heroes' victory still fails to agree on ownership. Mortal cooperation gives way to the six main campaigns.
objectives: Play all six protagonists and their six developed frontier towns on the unified master map.
Defeat six named commanders in three announced acts, with either order permitted within each pair.
Secure the central council island and ratify safe passage after the last commander falls.
routes: Act I: western/northern crossings; Act II: delta/eastern straits; Act III: northeastern/southern approaches to the island. Each act offers land and naval preparation routes. Previously opened routes stay open; inactive commanders defend fixed strongholds and do not receive hidden invulnerability.
water: At least two objective landings are ship-only; navy links distant armies faster than the outer land arc. Land armies fight commander battles after landing. Separate sea-monster encounters use only legal aquatic/flying rosters.
choice: Use the sanctuary reserves, defenses, canals, lights and intelligence inherited from P1–P6. Before each act, choose one front to receive the coalition's limited reserve. Both fronts remain winnable without it.
mark: The six roads and sea lanes become one recognized chart. The council island gains the Accord Stone and six vacant flag sockets. Defeated commanders are captured or accept surrender, not canonically killed before their main-campaign appearances.
later: The council ruins are the final objective in E7. Every surviving mark from P1–P6 helps the player recognize why this place mattered.
ending: The heroes sign a safe-passage pact. The gods will not sign a common claim. Final line: 'They had found one world. They had not agreed how to share it.'
target: 120–180 minutes across three saved acts; 6 commander battles plus at most 2 necessary sea encounters.
town: All six existing frontier towns retain their snapshot development. No seventh full faction town is introduced.

title: The Harbor We Once Saved
hook: Eighteen years after the First Accord, Alexios returns to First Harbor. Soldiers burn the last pieces of the longship to heat a checkpoint; his own old signature is still on the safe-passage stone.
story: Years of retaliatory wars have destroyed the frontier capitals. Alexios is ordered to reclaim the harbor from a Norse occupation. His victory is real, but it cuts the northern settlements off from imported grain.
objectives: Reclaim First Harbor's inhabited civic quarter and restart its first dwelling and shipyard.
Break the occupation through a ridge siege or naval supply interception followed by assault.
Capture the customs archive and decide how the harbor will treat enemy civilians.
routes: The P1 figure-eight survives as a ruined cliff road, quarry tracks and a partially flooded market. The preserved refuge/palisade provides a different flank. Two usable landing beaches prevent a single-port trap.
water: Interdict an occupation convoy or land behind the fort. At least one crossing is required to reach the archive island; keep a recoverable shipyard and a finite relief force.
choice: Requisition the grain for immediate military support, or release a protected civilian shipment. E2 still occurs; the choice changes famine pressure, a reserve and Hervor's dialogue, not whether her people deserve survival.
mark: Greek banners return to the harbor. A burned customs gate becomes either a military depot or civilian passage. The grain decision is written into the war ledger.
later: E2 starts with the convoy's arrival or its confiscation notice. E7 can use this harbor for either emergency supply or evacuation, based on its restoration.
ending: Alexios reads the old pact: 'No traveler shall pay for the quarrels of kings.' He orders the gates closed anyway—or opens one narrow exception.
town: Level-1 civic quarter inside the recognizable ruined First Harbor; higher tiers are nonfunctional ruins.

title: Bread across the Broken Fjord
hook: The convoy from First Harbor arrives under foreign conditions—or does not arrive. Hervor must feed Frostwatch while its inhabitants blame the allies she once trusted.
story: Hervor attacks the supply system supporting the new blockade. She is neither secretly evil nor mistaken about the suffering. The chapter lets the player understand why the previous victory creates another war.
objectives: Restore Frostwatch's granary and recruit a viable relief army.
Take two of three supply assets: grain island, bridge depot or captured transport anchorage.
Break the blockade command and secure a self-sustaining route before beginning the final assault.
routes: The P2 fjord ring persists, with wrecks, damaged piers and occupied watchtowers. Mountain supply is safer but slower; shipping is necessary to take the grain island. The earlier pass/channel improvement creates the alternate front.
water: Required sailing and one boarding battle against a supply ship, using two-ship combat. A monster-controlled outer route offers a different tactical risk.
choice: Return captured food under an armed exchange, or retain it and dismantle the enemy depot. One improves later trust; the other provides bounded defenses. Neither eliminates the grievances or skips E3.
mark: A liberated grain quay, dismantled depot and named memorial make the counteroffensive visible. No unexplained destruction of the entire region.
later: E5 can find Hervor's marked relief vessel among refugees. E7 inherits the fjord route and one modest reserve, not an unlimited stockpile.
ending: Hervor discovers that several armies now divert tribute toward the old council island. She assumes this is another pantheon's scheme.
target: 65–85 minutes; 4–5 required battles; visible logistics thresholds rather than a hidden starvation timer.
town: Frostwatch starts from its surviving hall and refugee huts; old high-tier buildings remain damaged scenery.

title: The Price of the River
hook: The gauges Seshet installed years ago now bear casualty tallies. Every opening of a sluice saves one settlement and deprives another army of its road.
story: Seshet retakes the delta to prevent its deliberate destruction. Her commanders demand that she withhold water from foreign districts. Records reveal that conquest rites—not ordinary fighting alone—are stressing the world's old seams.
objectives: Recover Sunbank and the original sluice ledger.
Take the two water-control strongpoints in either order, using an inland flank or island landing.
Defeat the army attempting to breach the embankment and preserve the two primary civilian water routes.
routes: The same three river arms remain, now crossed by siege roads and drowned fields. The P3 choice determines the initially sound canal or floodplain. A permanent ridge road prevents water changes from stranding the scenario.
water: Required island landings and a river-mouth sea encounter. Sluice previews show affected routes, and changing water requires all affected stacks to occupy legal fallback cells.
choice: Restore civilian irrigation first for refugee support, or the navigable canal first for a naval reserve. Both are ultimately restored enough to sustain life; there is no forced 'drown the innocent' choice.
mark: The delta regains water and fields, but abandoned siege works remain. A public water charter or military navigation marker records the player's priority.
later: E4 receives displaced families arriving through the reopened delta and must protect them across the old migration route. E7 benefits from the canal or civilian supply network.
ending: Seshet records: 'The river is not choosing sides. We are.' She sends copies of the evidence rather than trusting one god or ruler with it.
town: Sunbank's inhabited high ground is level 1; the former river palaces are flooded ruins.

title: The Ashes of the Living Arch
hook: Boats from Seshet's reopened delta arrive beneath the Living Arch carrying displaced families and weapons from both sides. A foreign army has turned Orla's old migration route into a gate for tribute caravans.
story: Orla fights to recover Hazel Ford and protect the groves, then finds evidence that her own side burned mixed settlements to deny them to enemies. She must stop a retaliatory expedition without pretending her opponents' earlier attacks never happened.
objectives: Secure the surviving Hazel Ford quarter and one evacuation route.
Recover the Living Arch by a woodland flank or coastal landing.
Defeat the expedition preparing to burn the remaining mixed sanctuary, then preserve its witnesses and records.
routes: The old forest loops remain legible through burned woods, regrowth and trenches. The sanctuary/road choice from P5 changes the safest approach, but both versions retain a land loop and a sea flank.
water: Ships offer an essential route to the sanctuary island and a useful rear landing. Optional Afanc hiring remains on legal land battle terrain; amphibious visuals do not grant new movement rules.
choice: Expose your own commanders' responsibility immediately for later civic trust, or secure their military stores before the hearing for a reserve at the cost of a colder council reception. The truth is preserved in both cases, not erased by the choice.
mark: One half of the arch is green, one half charred. A witness stone and reopened sanctuary become persistent markers. The player sees both repair and the cost of earlier war.
later: E6's records include Orla's evidence. E7 can draw on sanctuary volunteers or the recovered stores, with neither required for victory.
ending: Orla: 'We remember every tree they burned. We have forgotten the houses we burned beneath them.'
target: 65–90 minutes; 4–5 required battles; triggered defense rather than unbounded waves.
town: Hazel Ford survives as a hall and scattered shelters inside the old fort footprint.

title: The Fleet of Unlit Lanterns
hook: The paired lights Akane restored have gone dark by military order. Refugee ships carry lanterns hidden beneath their decks because visible light draws attacks.
story: Akane is ordered to capture the strait from a rival pantheon. Winning control reveals that every flag has used the passage to trap civilians and seize tribute. She opens a protected corridor while still fighting a genuine military opponent.
objectives: Restore Lantern Haven's shipyard and secure a replacement-vessel source.
Seize both sides of the strait through island assaults and defeat its finite blockade fleet.
Protect the declared departure of three registered civilian vessels; secure-route counters represent their progress rather than new bespoke escort mechanics.
routes: The P4 triangle is now a network of forts, wreck fields and a guarded inner channel. The chosen old lighthouse creates the safer opening. Outer water offers a monster encounter instead of a boarding battle, not a free bypass.
water: The most naval chapter: at least one boarding battle and one single-ship/sea-creature battle. Sea creatures remain in water or fly; ships carrying normal troops use the correct deck layout.
choice: Relight the inner light for protected evacuation or the outer light for fleet maneuver first. Both are eventually restored. The order changes one convoy's dialogue and a bounded reserve, not an unseen mass-casualty penalty.
mark: Both lights shine again; a wreck lane becomes a marked protected passage. Flags from multiple peoples hang at the landing, alongside the scars of the blockade.
later: E7 uses this passage for the joint landing and an evacuation alternative. P2/E2 relief-vessel flags provide a small recognizable callback.
ending: Akane intercepts six separate orders demanding the same conquest rite at the council island. They were issued independently, not by a single secret mastermind.
target: 75–100 minutes; 5 required battles; no endless sea-monster respawns.
town: Lantern Haven begins with its intact small shrine and rebuilt docks; military compounds remain ruined.

title: The Calendar of Scars
format: Final offensive and proof of the cost
hook: Itzel overlays the original six-sky record with the present heavens. Each major territorial consecration aligns with a new fracture. Her own victories are among them.
story: The collision's cause remains unknown. What can now be proved is that competing claims imposed upon its seams are destabilizing the merged world. This does not absolve anyone of choosing war. Itzel must fight her way to the records while her own leadership prepares another consecration.
objectives: Recover Ember Quay and the offshore observatory archive.
Defeat a rival occupation army and stop your own announced consecration convoy by capturing its staging stronghold.
Compare the six records and deliver copies to the protagonists, securing a limited emergency truce.
routes: The P6 volcanic horseshoe still defines the region. Wrecked bridges, ash fields and fortified quays change local movement. Two approaches reach the archive; its final island leg requires a ship. The old depot/observatory choice changes preparation benefits.
water: Required crossing to the archive and protection of the message route. A capped Hafgufa encounter can be avoided via a longer defended channel; neither route demands new creatures or artifacts.
choice: Commit the recovered tribute to emergency repairs or to the joint expedition's finite reserve. Both provide the proof and the truce; effects are shown before choosing.
mark: A visible fracture crosses the restored observatory courtyard. The old council platform is repaired for the six heroes; military banners are lowered only within the agreed neutral corridor.
later: E7 begins with these six signatures. The restored frontier towns are preserved, rather than being reset for the finale.
ending: Itzel: 'The sky did not learn to hate us. It learned the shape of our promises.' The agreement suspends conquest rites locally; it does not end every war.
target: 75–100 minutes; 5 required battles; no last-minute surprise loss timer.
town: Ember Quay starts from a surviving terrace settlement beneath the ruined older center.

title: The World We Leave Behind
format: Multi-front heroic finale and lasting settlement
hook: All six heroes return to the island where they once promised safe passage. Their armies now occupy opposite approaches, and military councils refuse to abandon the territorial claims purchased with years of blood.
story: The protagonists must defeat the forces sustaining incompatible conquest rites, hold open the shared routes and replace exclusive claims with a limited joint custodianship. These enemies defend political power, not mind control. The gods cannot fight directly; mortal heroes must carry the decision.
objectives: Control all six protagonists and their six rebuilt frontier towns; secure three regional anchors in any order.
Defeat the Crown Host at the council stronghold in a major siege after preparing its approaches.
Begin a clearly announced three-day stabilization: hold the council and two of three supply approaches against three finite, telegraphed counterattacks.
Ratify the world's local settlement only after the fighting and stabilization are complete.
routes: Three simultaneous fronts: the western road/river system, the eastern naval passage, and the northern ridge. Each anchor can be secured by a different hero, but no timed simultaneous six-hero tile puzzle is required. The final island needs ships; previously earned shortcuts reduce travel and create flanking choices.
water: The joint island landing and one supply approach are mandatory naval operations. A boarding battle and a separate sea-creature encounter provide distinct tactics. No surprise storm removes every ship or invalidates an embarked army.
choice: Choose Shared Custody (six maintained stations; future politics emphasize disputed cooperation) or the Open Passage Charter (a demilitarized island and dispersed stations; future politics emphasize local autonomy). Both stop the current rupture and prohibit exclusive rites here. Neither erases pantheons or makes one ruler owner of the world.
mark: The Accord Stone is repaired across its cracks. Six roads and the protected sea lane remain. The settlement creates either six small guardian stations or a public harbor and dispersed markers, all using existing architectural kits.
later: The campaign resolves the immediate war over this basin and keeps the saved towns alive. Outside its treaty boundaries, rivalries and unfinished obligations remain available for later campaigns.
ending: A final survey reveals a distant coastline absent from both the old and new charts. Its shore bears the same fracture pattern recorded on the first night. The original collision is still unexplained. Last line: 'At last, they had agreed where their world ended. Then the horizon moved.'
target: 150–210 minutes across saved acts; 7–9 consequential battles total, including optional-route substitutions rather than additional cleanup.
town: All six E1–E6 restored towns persist. The central stronghold is an objective location, not a new playable faction.
